saints.name: St. Claude de la Colombière
saints.title: Priest
saints.shortBlurb: A French Jesuit of luminous holiness, confessor of St. Margaret Mary and steadfast apostle of the Sacred Heart of Jesus…
biography: Born on 2 February 1641 at Saint-Symphorien-d'Ozon near Lyons, Claude de la Colombiere entered the Society of Jesus at seventeen and was ordained priest in 1669. After years of teaching and preaching, in 1675 he was made superior of the Jesuit house at Paray-le-Monial.

There he became confessor to Margaret Mary Alacoque, a Visitation nun who reported revelations of the Sacred Heart of Jesus. Where others doubted her, Claude discerned the hand of God, became her surest support, and gave the rest of his life to spreading the devotion.

In 1676 he was sent to England as preacher to Mary of Modena, Duchess of York. Caught up in the panic of the false 'Popish Plot,' he was arrested in 1678 and imprisoned for some weeks, saved from death by the protection of King Louis XIV but banished from England, his health broken.
He died at Paray-le-Monial on 15 February 1682, the first Sunday of Lent, worn out at the age of forty-one. He was beatified in 1929 by Pope Pius XI and canonized on 31 May 1992 by Pope John Paul II.
saints.knownFor: His guidance of St. Margaret Mary and the spread of devotion to the Sacred Heart.

sources.text: Vatican biography, Canonization of St. Claude de la Colombière (vatican.va)
